thread:
Jordan (Customer): Hey team — after we migrated traffic to the Private VPC gateway yesterday, our production API started returning 429s during short spikes. Not steady — bursts every ~10-15s where several hundred requests spike, and ~10-15% fail with 429. No change to app code. Anyone seen this with k8s ingress + gateway in front?

Jordan (Customer): Minimal log line: `2026-03-14T18:22:11Z GET /v1/generate 429 rate_limited gateway=private-vpc-01 client=10.2.4.12`

Liam (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the gateway/ingress rate-limit config and the k8s ingress controller type (nginx/contour/traefik)? also, do your clients respect `Retry-After`?

Jordan (Customer): Using nginx-ingress (controller v1.8.1) + an Envoy sidecar for internal routing. Ingress has these annotations right now:
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "1000"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "60000"  # we tried minutes -> maybe wrong granularity
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "50"
```
We also have a Red­wood private gateway with default caps. Clients do basic retry but with no jitter.

Maya (SRE): couple quick thoughts:
- NGINX `limit-rpm` is pretty coarse; prefer `limit-req` with a `zone` + `burst`/`nodelay` so token bucket semantics are correct. `limit-connections` is connection-based, not requests/sec.
- If your bursts are short (sub-second spikes), ingress `burst` needs to be large enough or you'll hit the limiter immediately.
- Check ip_conntrack and kube-proxy conntrack settings — conn exhaustion can manifest as 429/502 depending on proxy.

Maya (SRE): suggested ingress snippet (try on a green canary):
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-req-zone: "$binary_remote_addr zone=req_zone:10m rate=100r/s"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-req: "zone=req_zone burst=200 nodelay"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "2000"
```
Notes: set rate roughly to steady-state RPS per client IP, burst to cover 95th percentile spike. `nodelay` will reject only after burst is consumed.

Priya (CSE): also check the Redwood Private gateway rate limiter config — by default we apply a token-bucket per-customer and a global gate. If you have many clients behind a NAT or shared egress, they look like one client and exhaust the per-IP quota. For VPC gateways we can:
- enable `per-route` rate limits (route-level tokens)
- increase the `burst_capacity` for short spikes
- configure `shared_token_buckets` to shard across pods
We can propose settings to your account if you want.

Liam (Support): quick repro checklist for us to triage: 1) exact nginx annotation values; 2) `kubectl get pods -n ingress-nginx -o wide` (node distribution); 3) sample `curl -v` with repeated requests that trigger 429 (include headers); 4) gateway config from `/admin/ratelimit` or the console (screenshot okay).

Jordan (Customer): ok sending the curl trace and ingress pod list:
```
$ for i in {1..800}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.internal.example.com/v1/generate & done
# many 200s then a bunch of 429s, pattern every ~10s
```
Ingress pods across 3 nodes, CPU/NET not saturated. Adding `Retry-After` header on 429 would help clients.

ops-bot: Deployment redwood-private-gateway v2.14.1 rolled 2026-03-14T17:58:04Z — rate-limiter defaults: `per_customer_rate=200r/s`, `burst_capacity=100`.

Maya (SRE): ops-bot note explains it — your steady combined RPS across clients >200, bursts exceed the `burst_capacity=100`. With shared NAT you'll see token bucket exhaustion every spike. Two paths: bump gateway burst/rate or add per-source (IP or route) limits at the ingress so the gateway sees smoother traffic.

Liam (Support): for immediate mitigation we recommended (can do live with customer permission):
- Increase gateway `burst_capacity` to 2000 temporarily and `per_customer_rate` to 800r/s during peak window.
- On ingress, switch to `limit-req` zone as Maya suggested so clients can absorb short bursts locally.
- Add client retry jitter (exponential backoff with random jitter) so retries don't synchronize.

Priya (CSE): I can propose the Private gateway config change under your enterprise account and run it during low hours. Also recommend logging the `x-redwood-rate-limit` headers so we can correlate which limiter fired.

Jordan (Customer): we applied the ingress `limit-req` change (canary to 10% of traffic) and bumped `burst` to 300. After 20m we still saw a few 429s but much reduced. If you push the gateway bump we'll watch.

Maya (SRE): TL;DR config we used to verify locally:
```yaml
# nginx ingress annotations
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-req-zone: "$binary_remote_addr zone=req_zone:20m rate=250r/s"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-req: "zone=req_zone burst=1200 nodelay"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: "16k"
```
And on gateway: `per_customer_rate=800`, `burst_capacity=2000`, enable `x-rate-debug:true` in staging to capture which limiter responds.

Liam (Support): after customer confirmation we rolled the gateway bump (ops-bot confirmed). Monitoring dashboard shows 429 rate dropped from ~8% to <0.2% in the 30m window. :tada:

Jordan (Customer): confirmed — 429s gone, latency slightly up during big spikes but within SLA. We'll keep ingress `limit-req` and client backoff. Thanks! :heart:

Priya (CSE): follow-up items: 1) schedule a post-mortem to document config choices; 2) update runbook for private VPC customers migrating to ensure gateway defaults match expected steady-state RPS; 3) we should add a console callout about shared-NAT implications.

Maya (SRE): added runbook note and an ops checklist to `internal/priv-gateway-migration` (will ping when live).

Liam (Support): marking as resolved for now. If Jordan sees anything else ping this thread. :eyes:
